Published online:
September 11, 2026

Geographic focus:
United Kingdom, with secondary references to the Eurozone and global bond markets

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — July GDP data and recent bond yield moves
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — BoE rate decision next week, November hike pricing, energy price trajectory
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Rate path through mid-2027, BoE 2026 full-year growth forecast

Synopsis:
UK GDP surged 0.4% in July, well above flat expectations, with services leading the expansion. The UK led G7 growth in H1 2026 at 1%. However, rising energy costs driven by the Iran war are pushing bond yields to multi-decade highs globally — UK 10Y near 5.4%, 30Y near 6%. Markets are nearly fully pricing a BoE hike in November, with ~3 more hikes by mid-2027. BoE Governor Bailey is pushing back on automatic rate hike assumptions, framing market pricing as a risk premium rather than a policy signal. The pound edged up modestly on the GDP beat.
